items.title: Το Mercury 3 ισχυρίζεται ότι ξεπερνά το GPT-6 Luna, ο Claude Haiku 5,5 με 8 φορές μεγαλύτερη ταχύτητα
items.titleOriginal: Mercury 3 claims to outperform GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 at 8 times the speed
items.description: Η εταιρεία έρευνας και προϊόντων τεχνητής νοημοσύνης Inception με έδρα την Καλιφόρνια αποκάλυψε το Mercury 3, το πιο πρόσφατο μοντέλο γλώσσας διάχυσης, υποστηρίζοντας ότι ξεπερνά τους βελτιστοποιημένους σε ταχύτητα ανταγωνιστές GPT-6 Luna και Claude Haiku 5.5 σε μια σειρά σημείων αναφοράς ενώ τρέχει τέσσερις έως οκτώ φορές πιο γρήγορα. Το νέο μοντέλο παράγει περισσότερα από 1.000 token ανά δευτερόλεπτο σε ευρέως διαθέσιμη NVIDIA…
items.descriptionOriginal: California-based AI research and product company Inception has unveiled Mercury 3, its latest diffusion language model, claiming it outperforms speed-optimized rivals GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on a range of benchmarks while running four to eight times faster. The new model generates more than 1,000 tokens per second on widely available NVIDIA GPUs and supports a context window of 1 million tokens, allowing it to process substantially larger amounts of information in a single request. According to Inception, Mercury 3 is more than 40 times larger than its first-generation model, Mercury 1, while maintaining comparable processing speeds. The company says the results demonstrate that diffusion-based language models can become more capable without sacrificing the speed advantages of their underlying architecture. Scaling without sacrificing speed Traditional large language models generate text sequentially, predicting one token at a time. Diffusion language models take a different approach, generating and refining multiple tokens in parallel. This allows them to produce responses faster, potentially reducing delays in applications that require frequent interactions with a model. However, developers have traditionally faced a trade-off between model capability and response speed. Smaller models generally respond faster, while more capable systems often require additional processing time. Inception says Mercury 3 addresses this challenge by delivering performance comparable to or better than recently released OpenAI and Anthropic models across several standard benchmarks while maintaining inference speeds above 1,000 tokens per second. 1/4 Today, we’re releasing Mercury 3. Mercury 3 is by far our most powerful model and the most intelligent diffusion LLM ever released. It outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 on quality while running at 1000+ tok/sec. pic.twitter.com/TYevDl43Lm — Stefano Ermon (@StefanoErmon) October 19, 2026 The release marks the company’s fourth model since introducing Mercury 1 in June 2025. Mercury 2 subsequently introduced reasoning capabilities, while Mercury 2.5 added adjustable reasoning and expanded the context window to 260,000 tokens. Mercury 3 increases that capacity to 1 million tokens, nearly quadrupling the amount of information the model can handle at once. “Since we launched Mercury 1, the question we’ve heard most is whether diffusion can scale. Mercury 3 is over 40 times larger, significantly more capable, and still runs at over 1,000 tokens per second,” said Stefano Ermon, co-founder of Inception. Ermon added that the company has already begun training its next model. Faster responses for developers The company is targeting applications where response delays can affect usability, including interactive tutoring, live translation, writing assistants and automated software agents. In agent-based systems, models often perform multiple sequential tasks, such as searching websites, analyzing information or examining software logs. Delays at each stage can increase the time required to complete an operation. Inception says Mercury 3’s faster inference could help reduce these cumulative delays without requiring developers to switch to less capable models . Early-access customers are already testing the model in production workflows. Educational technology company RevisionDojo reported that Mercury 3 reduced response times for student feedback, including hints, definitions, and marked answers, to approximately one second. Mercury 3 is available through the Inception API, Baseten, OpenRouter, and Vercel. The model is compatible with the OpenAI API format, allowing developers to integrate it into existing applications without extensive code changes.

items.descriptionOriginal: Every couple argues . It might be about the dishes, the budget, raising kids, or dealing with the in-laws. Some fights are big, some are small. Most of the time, it blows over pretty fast. Disagreements are a natural part of sharing your life , your home, and your heart with another person. Occasionally, small misunderstandings quickly snowball into something larger . The kind of full-fledged, exhausting fight where nobody wins and both people walk away feeling hurt. Marriage and family therapists say there’s a surprisingly simple way to keep these disagreements from spiraling out of control. It’s called the partial concession. What is a partial concession? It’s exactly what it sounds like. You acknowledge the portion of the problem that you’re responsible for. You’re not conceding the whole argument, just your piece. It might sound something like “You’re right, I said I’d handle that, and I dropped the ball.” Or “I can see why what I said came across as dismissive.” At its core, a partial concession means stepping back and acknowledging the truth in what your partner says. That matters, even if you disagree with how your partner is framing the issue. You aren’t surrendering your whole argument. You’re just not pretending like you had nothing to do with it. Why it works First, it shows you’re actively listening. Your partner can tell you’ve actually heard and believed them, rather than just waiting for your turn to talk. The goal is to de-escalate and take oxygen away from the fire before emotions reach a point of no return. By validating your loved one’s points while holding space for your own, you transform a potential shouting match into a productive conversation. Once the pressure is reduced, it’s a lot easier to find a solution and move forward. The conversation can shift from “Whose fault is this?” to “What do we do now?” Research supports the effectiveness of a partial concession. In a study of 953 married or cohabiting couples, Baylor psychologist Keith Sanford found that when people feel blamed or criticized, they tend to want their partner to back off. That can mean admitting faults, showing respect, and being willing to compromise. Make it real, rather than just making a point A few tips make the difference between a real concession and a hollow one: Be specific. “Fine, I’m sorry you feel that way” doesn’t count. If you had committed to doing a task and forgot, admit your mistake. No one’s perfect, after all. Do it early. Don’t wait until you feel completely justified. You can release a lot of the steam from an argument by acknowledging your part sooner, rather than waiting until you feel you’ve said everything you want to get off your chest. Negotiate from a place of strength—being honest displays that strength. Don’t retreat entirely. You can concede a piece of an argument and still hold your ground on the rest. By acknowledging their valid points, you can turn a potential shouting match into a productive conversation. Relationships aren’t about keeping score or proving who is right. Sometimes, the smartest thing you can do is take a deep breath…and yield. Just a little bit. That way, you can build a sturdy bridge back to each other, where you wanted to be all along. The post Couples therapists say this simple move takes the heat out of almost any disagreement appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Ο ειδικός στο Charisma χρησιμοποιεί το «Ted Lasso» για να επεξηγήσει 6 στρατηγικές για τον χειρισμό της ασέβειας
items.titleOriginal: Charisma expert uses ‘Ted Lasso’ to illustrate 6 strategies for handling disrespect
items.description: Ο αριθμός των μαθημάτων ζωής που μπορεί κανείς να αντλήσει από τον Ted Lasso είναι αρκετά εντυπωσιακός, όπως μπορούν να επιβεβαιώσουν οι θαυμαστές. Η περίφημη σειρά που νιώθει καλά, γνωστή για την καρδιά και το χιούμορ της, προσφέρει μια τεράστια βοήθεια ψυχοσυναισθηματικής σοφίας τυλιγμένη σε ένα ταπεινό, λαϊκό πακέτο. Το δημοφιλές κανάλι YouTube Charisma on Demand έχει συγκεντρώσει και συσκευάσει μέρος αυτής της σοφίας σε ένα βίντεο…
items.descriptionOriginal: The number of life lessons one can glean from Ted Lasso is quite impressive, as fans can attest. The famously feel-good series, known for its heart and humor, offers a hefty helping of psycho-emotional wisdom wrapped in a humble, folksy package. The popular YouTube channel Charisma on Demand has compiled and packaged some of that wisdom in a video about how to handle disrespect. Most of us will, at some point, find ourselves on the receiving end of judgment, rudeness, passive-aggressive attacks, or other forms of disrespect. As Dr. Nina Ahuja writes in Psychology Today, disrespect can change us, affecting our willingness to speak up, our self-image, and our ability to recognize its impact over time. But with some conscious strategies, we can avoid letting disrespect derail us and even become “immune” to it. Charisma on Demand shared six ways to wisely handle disrespect, with examples from Ted Lasso (which you can watch in the video above): Remember disrespect isn’t about you Even though it can feel very personal, someone’s disrespect has nothing to do with you. “Sometimes it can be the other person’s insecurity or their fear, and sometimes it’s their need to feel superior,” the video states. “For many people, they’ve been using these defense mechanisms for so long that it’s simply just become a habit. Whatever the reason, it’s always coming from them, not you.” You aren’t responsible for the way someone else behaves, and what they do or say broadcasts something about them, not you. It’s easy to internalize anything that feels critical or negative toward us and start wondering what we need to change about ourselves. “Sometimes we become so convinced that we’re the ones to blame that we see disrespect where it wasn’t even intended,” the video points out. Assume positive intent “Sometimes it’s not obvious whether a comment is meant as an insult or if it’s just bad phrasing,” the video says. Either way, you can defuse a disrespectful statement by reacting as if the person had the best intentions. Ted’s character is a master at this. No matter what barbs other characters throw at him, he always responds as if their comments were neutral at worst. Relationship cheat code: Assume positive intent. That passive aggressive email? They were probably just rushed. Stinging feedback? They just want you to succeed. Don't assign sinister motives to innocent actions. Assuming the worst creates enemies. Assuming the best builds trust. — Dave Kline (@dklineii) December 2, 2025 However, there is a note of caution: “If insulting or passive-aggressive behavior persists, you can’t just keep assuming positive intent. If you keep pretending that you don’t see repeated disrespect, you end up being walked over. So assume positive intent once and then respond non-defensively.” People love to see a clapback, but as Charisma on Command points out, those kinds of zingers rarely work. Practice the art of non-defensive response The first step is simply to pause before responding. “Pausing for 5 to 7 seconds will give you a moment to breathe, which allows you to find the best response instead of just being reactive,” the video explains. “It’ll also force that person to sit with the comment they just made. And when they don’t get an immediate reaction from you, the silence can become very uncomfortable for them.” They may even walk back their comment after they’ve sat with it for a moment. Another non-defensive response is to go in the opposite direction and offer the person a compliment. “Now, this can sound counterintuitive, but complimenting someone who is disrespecting you can break that combative frame. It’s easy to fight with someone who is fighting back. It is much harder to fight with someone who is saying positive things about you.” Watch Ted do just that: Just make sure you find something genuinely complimentary to say, as forced praise can come across as either passive-aggressive or people-pleasing, which won’t help you. Set boundaries and enforce them Sometimes you need to draw a line and make sure someone doesn’t cross it without consequences. In fact, setting and keeping a boundary can help prevent a situation from escalating. “A strong boundary should be one clear sentence that focuses on what you are going to do if someone else persists or does something,” the video explains. “So, you might say, ‘If you keep making jokes about my appearance, I’m going to leave.’ Now, if the disrespect continues, there is no shame in walking away. And if you are repeatedly assuming positive intent, responding non-defensively, setting boundaries, and they’re still being disrespectful, the best thing that you can do is to remove yourself from that situation.” But always return to the first tip and remember: disrespect isn’t about you. If that’s true, what’s at the bottom of it? Get curious One of the greatest scenes in Ted Lasso is when Ted gives a little speech while playing darts with the show’s biggest antagonist, Rupert. He shares that the quote, “Be curious, not judgmental,” helped him realize every bully who’d ever underestimated him had lacked curiosity. Then he hit bullseyes on every shot, pointing out that Rupert hadn’t even asked if he’d played darts before challenging him to a contest. “Genuine curiosity is disarming,” the video points out. “Disrespectful people expect reaction or debate, not curiosity and connection. So, ask open questions. Try to understand their point of view, even if you don’t think you’ll agree with them…If you ask the right questions, you can uncover the source of their disrespect. Sometimes they’re lashing out simply because they’re having a bad day. Other times, there’s something deeper going on. So, once you’ve asked that open question, give them space to answer without interrupting.” Gaining a greater understanding of where they’re coming from can help you respond more to the person than to the behavior. Step in when someone else is being disrespected This last tip for dealing with disrespect is actually a way to gain respect. It’s one thing to handle disrespect when it’s aimed at you. However, if you’re witnessing someone else being disrespected, even someone disrespecting themselves, you need a more direct response. Even non-confrontational Ted stepped in when Rupert said something disrespectful to his ex-wife (and Ted’s boss and friend) at the bar. “Hey!” he interjected. “Better manners when I’m holding a dart. Please.” View this post on Instagram “This is what it looks like to be truly immune to disrespect,” the video says. “You’re not just unaffected by it. You’re strong enough to defend others from it, too. That is how you become the person that people genuinely respect.” Thank you, Ted Lasso and Charisma on Demand, for the valuable lessons. You can follow Charisma on Command for more tips like this. The post Charisma expert uses ‘Ted Lasso’ to illustrate 6 strategies for handling disrespect appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: We all want to live a long and healthy life. But as we enter our 60s and beyond, and a lifetime of choices and genetic luck begins to show, the issue becomes increasingly urgent. When it comes to longevity , our bodies give us many clues about how well they will age. The good news is that we can improve many risk factors, no matter our age. Healthcare expert shares good signs that someone over 60 will have longevity Neal Shah is a healthcare researcher, innovator, and advocate for health equity in aging populations. He’s also a wildly popular social media creator with nearly half a million followers on YouTube. He recently filmed a short video about the signs he sees that someone over 60 is in for a long, healthy life. 1. Walking speed “This is one of the most reliable predictors that doctors have to assess your health,” Shah says. “Multiple studies show that older adults who walk at a brisk, natural pace live significantly longer than slow walkers.” He says that our muscular health, heart health, and balance are reflected in our natural walking speed, which is what makes it such a powerful indicator. “If you can still walk with purpose, I think that’s a very good sign.” 2. Grip strength “How hard you can squeeze is a surprising window into your whole body’s strength,” Shah says, adding that poor grip strength is often associated with higher rates of heart disease and earlier death. Grip strength is easy to test and improve at home. Dead hangs, or hanging from a bar for as long as possible, are a great indicator—30 seconds for women and 60 seconds for men are great targets . With practice and repetition, anyone can improve their numbers and their overall strength and health. 3. Standing up from a seated position “Can you stand up from a seated position without using your hands to push off?” Shah asks. “This one simple move tests your leg strength and balance all at the same time.” Other, similar tests include standing up from sitting on the floor with minimal use of hands and knees. Why is balance so important for longevity? One big reason is that balance issues contribute to falls in older adults, and falls often result in injuries that can rob a person of their ability to independently care for themselves, as well as shorten their lifespan. Avoiding falls by maintaining good strength and balance is a major key to living a long and healthy life. 4. Overall balance The next sign underscores the need for balance by directly testing it. “Being able to stand on one leg for about 10 seconds is a strong marker of longevity. Research has linked the inability to do it with a higher risk of dying in the years that follow.” Shah reiterates that after age 65, falls become one of the biggest dangers for many adults. 5. Staying socially connected “People with strong friendships and regular connection live longer than people who are isolated.” It doesn’t mean it’s not okay to enjoy quiet and solitude, but avoiding loneliness is massively important for adults over 60. “Chronic loneliness is as damaging to your health as even smoking 15 cigarettes a day.” 6. Quantity of movement A lot of people—not just older adults—exercise for 30 or 60 minutes per day but remain sedentary for much of the rest of the time. Shah says what’s actually more important as we age is the amount of time we spend moving rather than the intensity. “The people who live the longest tend to move constantly in small ways. Things like gardening, standing up often, walking to the mailbox. It’s that steady all day movement that matters most.” You don’t need to be a triathlete to live a long and healthy life. In fact, gentler and more consistent movement may be the key. Shah adds that people over 60 shouldn’t panic if they don’t pass any of the above tests with flying colors. “Every single one of these things can be improved at any age,” he says. Depending on where you start, improvement might mean adding a gentle daily walk and gradually increasing your walking speed. It might mean practicing balancing on one leg or incorporating strength training to improve full-body power and conditioning. Or, it might mean filling your calendar with more time spent with family and friends. None of the items above are a death sentence for anyone, but together they paint an extremely accurate picture of overall health that we can use to live a longer and healthier life. The post Elder-care researcher reveals 6 powerful clues older adults will live a long life appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: NVIDIA has announced that JUPITER, Europe’s first exascale supercomputer, has completed a record-breaking quantum computing simulation, allowing researchers to explore and validate magic state cultivation. The 104-qubit simulation, described by NVIDIA as the largest comprehensive simulation of a fault-tolerant quantum computing system to date, ran on NVIDIA GH200 GPUs at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre in Germany. Magic states are essential for performing complex calculations on fault-tolerant quantum computers. However, producing them with sufficiently low error rates remains a major challenge. Traditional methods require substantial hardware resources, with some estimates suggesting that up to 95 percent of a quantum computer’s physical qubits could be dedicated to producing these states, leaving relatively few available for calculations. NVIDIA’s announcement comes days after Google reported that its Willow quantum processor achieved a 40-fold reduction in errors while preparing specialized quantum states. Unlike NVIDIA’s work, which uses classical supercomputing hardware to simulate quantum processes, Google’s experiment involved preparing magic states on an actual quantum processor. The two approaches address different challenges in developing fault-tolerant quantum computers, with simulations helping researchers evaluate designs before testing them on physical hardware. Simulating real-world quantum errors Last year, JUPITER simulated a full 50-qubit universal quantum computer under ideal, noiseless conditions, surpassing the previous 48-qubit record established by Jülich researchers in 2019 on Japan’s K computer. The latest 104-qubit simulation, however, accounts for realistic hardware noise, allowing researchers to examine how errors affect magic state cultivation. Unlike ideal simulations , which assume quantum operations can be performed without errors, the new work models the disturbances that physical quantum processors encounter during calculations. This provides a more realistic way to assess whether proposed methods can operate reliably under practical conditions. Germany knows how to build, and now it’s bringing that expertise to industrial AI. Tonight in Berlin, @JensenHuang and Chancellor @_FriedrichMerz discussed combining German engineering with NVIDIA AI to advance manufacturing and automotive. We’re also backing Germany’s… pic.twitter.com/9uwH0rYYLk — NVIDIA (@nvidia) October 19, 2026 By simulating the process under these conditions, NVIDIA researchers validated an advanced magic state cultivation approach, providing a way to test future improvements. The results could also help identify weaknesses in proposed designs and guide researchers toward more efficient methods before committing resources to building quantum hardware. Scaling across 8,192 GPUs For the new project, NVIDIA researchers first developed and tested their methods on a GB200 NVL72 system at the company’s Accelerated Quantum Research Center. They scaled testing from four GPUs to hundreds before moving to 8,192 GPUs on JUPITER. According to NVIDIA, the development work helped reduce simulation efforts from weeks to days. The team used NVIDIA’s cuQuantum software to optimize simulation performance and its CUDA-Q platform to model the fault-tolerant quantum circuit. The detailed simulation could allow researchers to predict how future quantum computing designs might perform before building physical hardware. This could reduce the need for repeated hardware testing and help accelerate the development of quantum applications in drug discovery, financial modeling and materials science. “Useful quantum computing will require fantastically complex, fault-tolerant systems — and understanding how they behave at scale is essential to building them,” said NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. “Our results from Jülich show how quantum processors and GPU supercomputers can work together to tackle research that would otherwise be out of reach, accelerating the discovery of transformative quantum applications.”

items.descriptionOriginal: Since 2021, the International Dog Photography Awards have given professional and amateur photographers alike a platform to showcase their artistic talent , celebrate beloved dog breeds , and shine a light on those that are often misunderstood. For the 2026 awards, Katie Brockman won Dog Photographer of the Year for her image of a pit bull sporting a newspaper crown and collar. The crown’s headlines read positively, including “Pit Bull Saves Family From Fire” and “Pit bull therapy dog teaches lessons, allays fears.” Meanwhile, the collar carries more negative headlines, such as “A time-bomb on a leash?” and “Words ‘pit bull’ have sparked hysteria.” The image, aptly titled Loved and Hated , clearly conveys the “complicated relationship” between humans and pit bulls and other “bully breeds.” Loved and Hated , Katie Brockman “The collar and chain represent breed bans, restrictions, and other ways pit bulls are punished simply for existing, while the crown and gentle hand represent the advocates who support and love the breed. Meanwhile, the dogs themselves are caught in the middle between the two sides,” explained Brockman. Brockman met Caldwell, her pit bull model, while volunteering at a shelter. He had been overlooked by adopters and developed behavioral issues, lessening his chances of adoption even further. By then, however, Brockman had “fallen in love” with the sweet and stoic pittie. She even bought a house to adopt him. “Where I live, it’s nearly impossible to find rentals that allow bully breeds,” she noted. Brockman submitted to the Studio category, which focuses on controlled lighting and creative work produced inside a photography studio. Here are the other winners of the studio category: 2nd Place: Head in the Clouds , Jill Garrett Head in the Clouds , Jill Garrett 3rd Place: This is Growing Up , Belinda Richards This is Growing Up , Belinda Richards There are five other categories: Portrait Outdoor, Action, Dogs and People, Documentary, and Open. Keep scrolling to see the winner of these categories. Portrait Outdoor This category captures dogs in close-up portraits or expansive natural landscapes exclusively outdoors. 1st Place: Beyond The Track , Elena Marchi Beyond The Track , Elena Marchi 2nd Place: The hunter becomes the hunted , Susan Lang The hunter becomes the hunted , Susan Lang 3rd Place: It’s Her World , Karir Laiapea It’s Her World , Karir Laiapea Action This category highlights dogs’ physical energy, movement, and athletic ability. 1st Place: Winter Launch , Nika Kuplenk Golobič Winter Launch , Nika Kuplenk Golobič 2nd Place: Mission Balance , Gavriella Leon Mission Balance , Gavriella Leon 3rd Place: Weightless , Linda Glomb Weightless , Linda Glomb Dogs and People This category emphasizes the unique connection, bond, and shared moments between dogs and their human companions. 1st Place: Close , Sarah Ebner Close , Sarah Ebner 2nd Place: Nika and Sherry , Eco Lorka Evoto 3rd Place: The Weight of Connection , Santos Román The Weight of Connection , Santos Román Documentary This category tells real-life, untold stories, rescue journeys, or emotional narratives (no AI-generated content allowed). 1st Place: Waiting , Tianhang Zhang Waiting , Tianhang Zhang 2nd Place: On top of the world , Katie Gyltnes On top of the world , Katie Gyltnes 3rd Place: Alone together , Katie Gyltnes Alone Together Dog Photography Awards, photo, winner , Katie Gyltnes Open This category allows creative, conceptual, and experimental dog photography styles. 1st Place: Run , Elena Marchi Run , Elena Marchi 2nd Place: Losing Control , Callie Soden Losing Control , Callie Soden 3rd Place: Swimming , Tianhang Zhang Swimming , Tianhang Zhang The post See the 18 incredible finalists of the 2026 Dog Photography Awards-including one profound pit bull appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Though it’s hard for some of us sweltering through 100-degree weather to fathom, winter is fast approaching. That means it’s almost time to pull those forgotten winter coats out of storage , where they may be hiding some unexpected joy in their pockets…as comedian Alice Etches so charmingly demonstrated. In the video, which has racked up over 6.4 million views since she shared it on social media, Etches puts on her coat for the first time since last year and quickly discovers she’s forgotten quite a few things tucked away. What’s in the pocket? At first she finds the usual suspects: an old lip balm, some tissues, a used train ticket from a “good weekend.” But then things get a little more unhinged as she pulls out a whisk, a TV remote (“I’ve been looking for that!) and a still-ripe pear, which is understandably baffling. Then she fully commits to the slapstick, producing an unopened DVD box set and a string of Christmas lights before quickly handing them to an imaginary person offscreen to keep rummaging. Finally, she reaches her last discovery. “It’s very soft,” she notes, struggling to retrieve whatever is hiding inside. “Oh, it’s sharp. It’s…” she says before pulling out a black cat. A cat?! “Buttons?” she exclaims in shock. “Oh, my God!” she says, holding it closer. “We thought you ran away! I’ve been looking all over for you!” Judging from the comments, Ethces is far from the only one to experience this very specific type of seasonal joy. People quickly shared stories of lost, forgotten items resurfacing in their winter coat time capsules. Strange items folks have found in their winter coat pockets “Faded receipt and a dog poo bag.” “Found a fork in my jacket pocket once. Still not sure what I was doing with it.” “Don’t forget ancient chewing gum.” “And a cough sweet stuck inside sometimes.” “Literally found $4, my ‘lost’ favorite earrings, a lipstick (not mine), and my transpo cards in a coat pocket the other day.” “The amount of surgical masks I have found in my various pockets over the years is astronomical.” “Everything but money.” Etches has more fun comedy skits where that came from From her “ Lady at the Farmer’s Market ,” who always promises to come back and make a purchase after “making a look” (spoiler alert: she never does): To that one “ friend who doesn’t know how to act around kids ”: To the woman who “ can’t relax on vacation ”: She clearly has a talent for finding silliness in everyday situations. Give her a follow and find more reasons to smile. Now, time to rummage through some pockets… The post Comedian captures the mysterious joy of checking the pockets in an old winter coat for the first time appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Many people find making small talk to be an excruciating experience. They think it’s boring to talk with a stranger about the weather, sports, or weekend plans. They may also feel like they don’t have anything to contribute to the conversation , or they don’t understand the point of having one in the first place. However, those who excel at making small talk have a tremendous advantage in their professional and romantic relationships , as well as in forming new friendships . Most importantly, small talk is a window to transition into medium talk or, eventually, deep, meaningful conversations. The problem is that many people get stuck in small talk, and things stall before progressing to something beneficial. A man and woman chatting. u200bvia Canva/Photos How to get better at small talk The great thing is that, like anything, making small talk is a skill that we can all improve by learning some simple conversation techniques. One technique that is great for keeping a conversation going, like hitting a ball back and forth past a net in tennis, is a simple statement: It reminds me of…” A redditor named IsaihLikesToConnect shared some great examples of how the phrase can be used to turn a mundane topic, such as the weather, into something much more fun. Them: “It’s been really rainy, huh?” You: Option 1 (Personal Story): “Yeah, it reminds me of a time I went on a run in the rain and nearly got hit by a car.” Option 2 (Music / Pop Culture): “It reminds me of every Adele song. When I’m driving, I feel like I’m in a music video.” Option 3 (Family): “It reminds me of my dad, he used to love playing with us in the rain as kids.” Option 4 (Thing you watched / World News): “It reminds me of this documentary I saw where they’re trying to make it rain in the Sahara Desert.” Option 5 (Place you lived): “It reminds me of when I lived in Australia, it barely ever rained there. I actually love this weather.” Coworkers having a conversation. u200bvia Canva/Photos You see in this example that using “It reminds me of…” opened up the conversation to five potential new and more exciting topics. The “You” in the story could have responded with, “Yeah, it sure is rainy,” and the conversation would have ended right there. But instead, branching off the topic of rain into something a bit deeper took the conversation to the next level. You get extra points if you can take the “reminds me of” into a topic that you assume the other person will be interested in. Coworkers having a conversation. u200bvia Canva/Photos What’s a polite way to change the topic in a conversation? Using “this reminds me of…” is also a polite way to move the topics in another direction, especially when it’s a topic that you don’t want to discuss or one that makes you feel a bit uncomfortable. Or, if it’s a situation where the other person is monologing on one topic for a very long time, this makes it easy to transition away from their diatribe. Ultimately, the phrase is an excellent way for you to save the person you’re talking to from being stuck in the small talk rut as well. It shows you understand that when someone brings up the weather, they are merely getting things started with something both of you have in common. They probably don’t want to talk about the weather for 30 minutes, unless they are a meteorologist. “It reminds me of…” is an invitation to go a bit deeper and shows the other person that you’d like to learn more about them. This article originally appeared in April. This article originally appeared 1 year ago. It has been updated. The post The 4 words that can keep conversation flowing forever, even between socially awkward people appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Generation X (those born between 1965-1980) grew up eating classic Americana meals. During the 1970s, comfort meals like tuna casserole and salmon roquettes were popular meals. Gen X also grew up eating some pretty unhinged (but all the more yummy) sandwiches. These meals are steeped in childhood nostalgia . And to this day, Gen Xers are still fond of their favorite dishes they grew up eating. Together, they discussed on Reddit their most-loved home-cooked dishes that they still whip up, starting with sloppy joes. Here are 17 iconic Gen X comfort meals to keep in mind the next time you make dinner: @genx_shawn Top 10 Things ONLY GenX Knows the Taste Of… #genx #over50club #genxtiktok #over40 #genxcrew #generationx #genxers #genxtok #over40club #over50 ♬ original sound – Shawn | GenX “Breakfast. We will have a ‘breakfast for dinner’ at least a couple times a month. Yum!” – fadeanddecayed, KddKc “Pizza bread! My mom would cut Italian bread into pieces, put butter and garlic salt on them, then pour some spaghetti sauce on them, cover with mozzarella cheese, and broil for like ten or fifteen minutes. Super easy and quick to make and so tasty. I’m sure my mom loved that I was so into something that took roughly zero effort for her to make.” – hornybutired “Grilled cheese and soup.” – reincarnateme “ Meat loaf. I use 2 pounds ground beef, replace bread crumbs with minute rice, add 1 pkg beef soup flavoring, chop an entire onion for it, and mix BBQ sauce into mixture. Oh, important: do not overmix! Place all ingredients into bowl, then mix quickly 10 or 12 swirls of a large spoon. Grease loaf pan, carefully place mixture in, pat down & bake about an hour. (Extra info: for even better flavor, mix the night before, pat into loaf pan, cover with plastic, put into fridge overnight. Remove from fridge about an hour before baking. BE SURE TO REMOVE PLASTIC WRAP! [Esp. If in Pyrex glass loaf pan])” – jehardt, AbbyM1968 “White guy tacos.” – najing_ftw “Skillet dinner. Kielbasa, bell pepper, onion, spuds in a cast iron pan. One dish. Easy peasy.” – UnimportantOutcome67 “Chicken pot pie or chicken ala king.” – sattersnaps “Fried catfish, greens, and red beans and rice.” – User Unknown “Shepherds pie, technically cottage pie if it’s ground beef. Homemade enchiladas, usually made as a layered casserole instead because I don’t have time to roll them. Pork chops with mashed potatoes and veggies.” – XerTrekker “Fried rice with chicken or pork leftovers.” – AlternativeResort181 “Hot hamburgers: hamburger patty open face on Texas toast thickness bread, cover with fries then cover that with brown gravy. Wife’s variation is hamburger patty over rice with brown gravy.” – EnricoMatassaEsq @past_archives American Gen X Foods That Kids Today Can’t Understand #nostalgia #childhoodmemories #backtochildhood #90s #2000s #usa #80s #90skids #80schildhood #capcutforus #capcut #capcutpioneer #America ♬ original sound – Past Archives “Stuffed peppers. I make it much more easily by cooking it all in one large frying pan ‘deconstructed’. Sauté onions garlic and ground beef, add cut up peppers, tomatoes or tomato sauce, sometimes a little spinach, then add separately cooked rice, salt and pepper and serve. It comes together pretty quickly and tastes just as good as stuffing and baking peppers in the oven.” – Affectionate-Map2583 “Macaroni and cheese with cut up hot dogs. Seriously, that’s what I ate tonight.” – Dazzling-Walrus9673 “Homemade Stroganoff casserole. Ridiculously easy to make. Ingredients: 1.25-1.5 lbs. Ground Beef 1 each of large white onion, green pepper, and red pepper 1 can mushroom pieces, drained and rinsed 12 oz. Bag of wide egg noodles 1 can cream of mushroom soup 16 oz. Sour cream Worcestershire Sauce Louisiana Hot Sauce White or Black Pepper Panko bread crumbs To Make: Preheat oven to 360 degrees. Worcestershire, hot sauce, garlic powder, and pepper are all to taste, depending on how much flavor and punch you want it to have. Cook noodles per instructions. Drain. Peel and slice onion (not diced), core and cut peppers into strips Brown meat, onions and peppers along with liberal amount of Worcestershire; garlic, pepper, and hot sauce. Add mushrooms. Cook until meat is fully brown, onions are translucent and peppers are tender. Drain. Combine drained meat, etc. with whole can of soup, half of the sour cream. Gradually add noodles into the mix. Add sour cream as needed to maintain consistency. Add Worcestershire, hot sauce, and pepper to taste. Dump into large, deep Corning dish or whatever. Cover too with bread crumbs. Cover and bake for forty minutes.” – CynfullyDelicious This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. Αυτός είναι πιθανώς ο μόνος λόγος που υπάρχουν τα φόρουμ για γάτες, αλλά ένα παιδί που χρειαζόταν ένα επιστημονικό έργο στην 6η τάξη αποφάσισε να παραλείψει τα φόρουμ για τις γάτες για απαντήσεις και αντ' αυτού να χρησιμοποιήσει την επιστημονική μέθοδο. Ο Kaeden Henry, ένας μαθητής της έκτης δημοτικού που ζει στη Φλόριντα, σκέφτηκε γενναία μια ερώτηση…
items.descriptionOriginal: Cat owners sometimes have unique questions that even Google doesn’t always have the answer to. This is probably the sole reason cat forums exist, but one kid who needed a 6th grade science project decided to skip the cat forums for answers and instead use the scientific method. Kaeden Henry, a sixth grader living in Florida, bravely pondered a question few (if any one) has been brave enough to ask: do cat buttholes touch every surface they sit on? Since cats do whatever the heck they want , training them not to jump on kitchen counters is a feat even Hercules struggles to complete. These fierce felines don’t care if you’re cooking dinner or trying to get comfy in bed. If they want to sit somewhere, they’re going to do it. The thought of cat butts on that expensive Serta pillow designed to feel like you’re sleeping on a cloud can gross people out, but thanks to Kaeden, you no longer have to wonder if the butthole itself is also making contact. The curious sixth grader is homeschooled and well-versed in the scientific method thanks to her mother’s PhD in animal behavior with a concentration in feline behavior. And, since they own cats, the science experiment was pretty straightforward (and directly impactful). To complete the experiment, Henry and his mom, Kerry Hyde, bought non-toxic lipstick and applied it to each of their cat’s anuses. Then, the cats were given commands. “Non-toxic lipstick was applied to their bum-bums, they were then given a series of commands (sit, wait, lie down, and jump up. Side note: Both cats have been trained since kittenhood with a variety of commands, they also know how to high-five, spin around, and speak.), they were compensated with lots of praise, pets, and their favorite treats, and the lipstick was removed with a baby wipe once we collected our data in just under 10 minutes,” Hyde wrote in a Facebook post. The results? Turns out that, no, cat buttholes do not touch every surface cats sit on. Now, let’s all take a collective sigh of relief while we go over the details. Kaeden’s experiment covered long-haired, short-haired, and medium-haired cats (if your cat is hairless, you better stock up on Clorox wipes just in case). “His results and general findings: Long and medium haired cat’s buttholes made NO contact with soft or hard surfaces at all. Short haired cats made NO contact on hard surfaces. But we did see evidence of a slight smear on the soft bedding surface. Conclusion, if you have a short haired cat and they may be lying on a pile of laundry, an unmade bed, or other soft uneven surface, then their butthole MAY touch those surfaces!” Hyde shares. Now every curious cat owner can rest easy knowing that as long as their cat has hair, their bare bottom balloon knot is not touching the majority of surfaces in their home. The amusing experiment caught the Internet’s attention. People laughed and commented, with one person writing, “This is probably the most useful information I’ve learned from a science fair project.” “Good to know!…I can now eat my sandwich left on the counter with confidence!” another writes. “A+++!!! Whew!! I am very grateful for your sciencing on this subject. My fears from walking in on my cat sitting on my laptop keyboard and subsequently being grossed out and cleaning furiously in a hyper-ocd manner have been somewhat allayed and now maybe I won’t have to use QUIIITE so many wipes.” someone chimes in. “Finally.. Someone answers the important questions!!” This article originally appeared in April This article originally appeared 1 year ago. It has been updated. The post 6th grader’s science experiment answers, ‘Do cat buttholes touch every surface they sit on?’ appeared first on Upworthy .

Το νέο τσιπ υπολογιστή Super Intelligence (SI) σχεδιάστηκε από ερευνητές στο Εθνικό Εργαστήριο Brookhaven (BNL) του Υπουργείου Ενέργειας των ΗΠΑ (DOE). Για το έργο, οι πα…
items.descriptionOriginal: Scientists in the state of New York have created a first-of-a-kind superconducting neural chip that can reportedly process about one million fusion plasma samples per second. The new Super Intelligence (SI) computer chip was designed by researchers at the US Department of Energy’s (DOE) Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL). For the project, they partnered with the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL), the DIII-D National Fusion Facility, and Colorado-based tech company Great Sky. BNL noted that the chip relies on superconducting circuits to mimic human neural networks. It could eventually improve the way fusion reactors monitor and control hot plasma. Lab tests showed the chip could detect unusual plasma behavior and predict instabilities. “It’s incredible to see the team processing data from our tokamak with this first-of-a-kind chip,” Richard Buttery, PhD, DIII-D Director, said. The team believes the technology could support faster and more reliable fusion reactor control systems. Handling plasma data Fusion reactors use magnetic fields to keep hot plasma confined at temperatures between 180 and 270 million degrees Fahrenheit (100 and 150 degrees Celsius). This extreme temperature is roughly 10 times hotter than the core of the Sun. Still, plasma conditions can change rapidly, making real-time monitoring essential to keep it stable. This requires computers that can process huge amounts of data almost instantly. But conventional silicon-based computing systems struggle to process such large amounts of data quickly enough. The wafers in the first-of-a-kind chips mimic human brain networks. Credit: Great Sky Inc. However, the novel superconducting neural chip can process signals at extremely high speeds. It uses superconducting circuitry arranged to mimic the connections found in the human brain. To test it, the scientists collected data from the DIII-D tokamak, a fusion research facility run by General Atomics in California. Two of these tests assessed the chip’s ability to spot unusual plasma activity and predict disruptions. The data were collected at a rate of one million samples per second, and the chip successfully handled the pace. “This is a powerful new platform for implementing many of the SI algorithms our team at Brookhaven Lab is developing,” Shinjae Yoo, PhD, CDS AI department chair and the project’s principal investigator, said. Plasma instabilities In addition, a third experiment conducted by the team, involved simulated plasma data generated by TORAX . The system is a differentiable tokamak core transport simulator developed by Google DeepMind’s fusion team. During the experiment, the chip analyzed signals to predict the onset of sawtooth instabilities, which involve rapid changes in plasma conditions. The results showed that superconducting neural networks could potentially support real-time plasma monitoring and stabilization. Steven Cowley, PPPL director, stressed the importance of creating faster control systems for fusion reactors. “We are building the fusion machines of the SI era ,” he added. “This chip took data straight from a tokamak at millions of samples every second and kept up.” Great Sky stated that the device is its largest superconducting neural chip to date. Similar chips could reportedly find use in quantum computing, cybersecurity, and high-speed X-ray data analysis. At present, the team is developing a new chip with a neural network 10 times larger than the current design. They plan to present the hardware at BNL in early 2027, before it undergoes testing at the DIII-D tokamak during fusion experiments later that year. “This is just the beginning,” Jeff Shainline, Great Sky founder and CEO, concluded in a press release . “This approach to AI hardware has so much to offer with regard to fusion, as well as other applications at the forefront of technology.”

items.descriptionOriginal: Η Τερψιχόρη Σαββάλα είναι καλλιτέχνις — κάνει κεραμικά και ζωγραφίζει. Οι σπουδές της στην ιστορία και την αρχαιολογία της έμαθαν να ψάχνει τους συμβολισμούς στα μοτίβα που βλέπει από την αρχαιότητα μέχρι τη νεότερη λαογραφική τέχνη. Mοτίβα του 800–700 π.Χ. που επανεμφανίζονται, αναλλοίωτα, στα κεντήματα των Ελληνίδων γιαγιάδων — σχέδια που επέζησαν από την αρχαιότητα μέχρι τη λαϊκή τέχνη, χωρίς να θυμάται κανείς από πού ξεκίνησαν. Το αγαπημένο της παράδειγμα είναι το γοργόνειο: το αποτρόπαιο πρόσωπο στην ασπίδα της Αθηνάς, που αργότερα ονομάστηκε Μέδουσα· μια αρχαία μητέρα-θεά, χθόνια επειδή η γονιμότητα έρχεται κάτω από το έδαφος, τρομακτική μόνο προς τον εχθρό, πάντα εκεί για να προστατεύει το τέκνο της ή όποιον τη φοράει. Διαβάστε επίσης Η Τερψιχόρη Σαββάλα που συμμετέχει με έργο της στη δεύτερη Biennαle of Contemporαry Kerαmics στη Ρόδο μιλάει για την παράδοση ως έμπνευση, ως ταυτότητα, ως συνέχεια, ως κληρονομιά με την ίδια έννοια που είναι η γενετική: τα μοτίβα, η αισθητική, το σεμεδάκι κάτω από την τηλεόραση — κάτι από το οποίο δεν μπορείς να ξεφύγεις όσο κι αν θέλεις. Στην καρδιά του νέου short doc είναι η επιστροφή μας στην παράδοση και η σημασία της τάσης αυτής όπως μας την εξηγεί η καλλιτέχνις. items.descriptionOriginal: Δύο ημέρες γεμάτες θετική ενέργεια, χαμόγελα και, πάνω απ’ όλα, ανθρώπους πρόθυμους να προσφέρουν. Για ένα ολόκληρο διήμερο, η Θεσσαλονίκη έγινε μια μεγάλη αλυσίδα αλληλεγγύης, καθώς φοιτητές, κάτοικοι και επισκέπτες της πόλης ανταποκρίθηκαν στο κάλεσμα του προγράμματος εταιρικής υπευθυνότητας Allwyn Care για εθελοντική αιμοδοσία και εγγραφή εθελοντών δοτών μυελού των οστών. Από την Πολυτεχνική Σχολή του Αριστοτελείου Πανεπιστημίου Θεσσαλονίκης, την Παρασκευή 9 Οκτωβρίου, μέχρι τη Νέα Παραλία Θεσσαλονίκης, το Σάββατο 10 Οκτωβρίου, ο κόσμος έδωσε το δικό του αποτύπωμα στη διήμερη δράση. Άνθρωποι διαφορετικών ηλικιών βρέθηκαν στα δύο σημεία, ενημερώθηκαν και, κυρίως, επέλεξαν να προσφέρουν. Η διήμερη δράση διοργανώθηκε από το πρόγραμμα εταιρικής υπευθυνότητας Allwyn Care και τους οργανισμούς Bloode και Choose Life, σε συνεργασία με την 4η Υγειονομική Περιφέρεια Μακεδονίας και Θράκης, το Πανεπιστημιακό Γενικό Νοσοκομείο Θεσσαλονίκης ΑΧΕΠΑ και το Γενικό Νοσοκομείο Θεσσαλονίκης «Ιπποκράτειο», με τη στήριξη του Αριστοτελείου Πανεπιστημίου Θεσσαλονίκης και του Δήμου Θεσσαλονίκης. Η εθελοντική αιμοδοσία πραγματοποιήθηκε με στόχο την ενίσχυση των αποθεμάτων αίματος του Πανεπιστημιακού Γενικού Νοσοκομείου Θεσσαλονίκης ΑΧΕΠΑ και του Γενικού Νοσοκομείου Θεσσαλονίκης «Ιπποκράτειο», συμβάλλοντας στην κάλυψη αναγκών ασθενών που χρειάζονται άμεσα μετάγγιση. Παράλληλα, στο πλαίσιο της δράσης, το Choose Life ενημέρωσε και ευαισθητοποίησε το κοινό γύρω από τη δωρεά μυελού των οστών και τη διαδικασία εγγραφής εθελοντών δοτών, αναδεικνύοντας πόσο απλό μπορεί να είναι το πρώτο βήμα, για να προσφέρει κάποιος μια ευκαιρία ζωής σε έναν συνάνθρωπό του. Από πόλη σε πόλη, η προσφορά γίνεται πράξη Η δράση στη Θεσσαλονίκη αποτελεί μέρος της ευρύτερης προσπάθειας του Allwyn Care να συμβάλλει στην καλλιέργεια μιας σταθερής κουλτούρας εθελοντικής προσφοράς. Σε συνεργασία με τους οργανισμούς Bloode και Choose Life, το πρόγραμμα ταξιδεύει σε όλη την Ελλάδα, δημιουργώντας ευκαιρίες για όλο και περισσότερους ανθρώπους να συμμετέχουν έμπρακτα. The post Από το ΑΠΘ μέχρι τη Νέα Παραλία, η Θεσσαλονίκη έγινε μια αλυσίδα προσφοράς appeared first on POPAGANDA .

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News How Commercial Buildings Can Reduce Energy Use and Lower Operating Costs Reading Time: 3 minutes How Commercial Buildings Can Reduce Energy Use and Lower Operating Costs Commercial buildings waste about 30% of their energy, and that’s just an average, according to the U.S. Department of Energy. In practice, that means part of your utility bill is probably paying to heat empty rooms, cool unoccupied offices, light parking lots after everyone has gone home, or keep equipment running on an outdated schedule. While that’s a remarkably high number for energy waste, it’s surprisingly easy to lower it significantly. Often, you can start with low-cost fixes before investing in more sustainable and energy-efficient upgrades. All that is really needed is a fresh, honest look at how the building actually operates. Find Out Where Most of the Waste Goes Before replacing any equipment, look at your data: where does the building actually use energy? Review your utility bills, demand charges, operating schedules, and, where available, interval data from smart meters. Look specifically at peak demand times; staggered startup schedules can significantly reduce demand charges. Also compare energy use against occupancy and production schedules. If consumption barely changes between a busy Monday and an empty Sunday, something deserves investigation. An energy audit or retro-commissioning study can take this further. In plain terms, you are checking whether the building still operates the way its designers intended. Get Serious About Building Controls According to the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), high-performance control strategies can reduce annual HVAC energy use by 30% across a range of commercial building types. Of course, this doesn’t mean every building will cut its HVAC bill by that exact amount, but it shows why controls deserve more attention than they usually get. Look at temperature setbacks, occupancy schedules, ventilation rates, economizer operation, and simultaneous heating and cooling. A building automation system is only as useful as its programming. If the system has sophisticated controls but nobody checks whether they still match actual occupancy, you have an expensive computer making the wrong decisions. Upgrade Lighting and Control It LED retrofits remain one of the more straightforward commercial efficiency projects, particularly in buildings with old fluorescent or high-intensity fixtures. But swapping fixtures and calling the job finished misses half the opportunity. Add occupancy sensors where spaces sit empty for long periods. Use daylight controls near windows and skylights. Put exterior and parking-lot lighting on appropriate schedules rather than relying on someone to remember to flip a switch. This is also where electrical expertise matters. Whether you operate a warehouse in Texas, an office in Colorado, or need an Albuquerque electrical contractor for a New Mexico facility, look for a provider that can handle both the electrical work and efficiency side of the project. Look Beyond the Big Systems Some of the easiest savings are hidden in ordinary equipment. Plug loads can become a significant energy drain in efficient buildings, particularly where computers, kitchen equipment, vending machines, and other devices remain powered outside working hours. Smart power strips, automatic shutdown schedules, and better equipment procurement can help. This is a good reason to use submeters in larger facilities. Instead of seeing one enormous monthly electricity number, you can separate major loads and identify what changed. Use Maintenance as an Energy Strategy A dirty filter, poorly calibrated sensor, worn weatherstripping, or failing motor doesn’t just create a maintenance problem. It can make equipment work harder and longer. Build energy checks into preventive maintenance rather than waiting for an obvious failure. Inspect: HVAC controls and sensor calibration, Lighting and setback schedules, Equipment operating outside occupied hours, Door seals and building envelope air leaks, Unusual shifts or spikes in consumption. DOE research has found that properly tuned controls alone can produce substantial savings, partly because controls in existing buildings often drift away from their intended settings over time. Not every green upgrade deserves a blank check. Rank projects by expected energy savings, installation cost, maintenance savings, useful life, demand reduction, and available utility incentives. Inspired by her mother, Ratnabali believes art is about making people feel welcome, valued and less alone. Even as age and arthritis make her work harder, she refuses to give up. Μετά έρχεται άλλη αμφιβολία και άλλη. Σε μια αγροτική τάξη του Uttar Pradesh, αυτές μπορεί να φαίνονται σαν συνηθισμένες ερωτήσεις. Αλλά για την Αρχάνα, κάθε παιδί που νιώθει αρκετά άνετα να ζητήσει από έναν αντιπρόσωπο…
items.descriptionOriginal: "Archana ma'am!" The voice comes from one corner of the classroom. "Ma'am, I have a question." Another hand goes up. Archana Jaisal turns, listens and answers. Then comes another doubt, and another. In a rural Uttar Pradesh classroom, these may seem like ordinary questions. But to Archana, every child who feels comfortable enough to ask one represents something bigger: the opportunity to learn close to home. It is the kind of classroom she wished more village children could have. She knows what it means when education depends on circumstances : whether a family can afford coaching, whether a good teacher is nearby, or whether someone offers the right opportunity at the right time. "I realised that the children were studying, but their studies were not really helping them," she recalls of what she saw in villages. Inspired by her late father, Jagdish Ram, who studied while pulling a rickshaw, Archana grew up seeing how education can change a family's future. That realisation eventually led her to start Shiksha Saathi, a rural education and livelihood startup that now runs over 78 learning centres across six districts of Uttar Pradesh, reaching more than 7,650 students with 67 teachers. But the story began long before the first centre opened. It began with her late father, Jagdish Ram. From rickshaw puller to railway employee Archana grew up in Ghazipur, where her father's own childhood had been shaped by hardship. Her grandfather died when her father was young, leaving the family struggling to survive. There was also pressure to get his sisters married. With little money coming in, her father had to make a difficult choice. At 17, he began pulling a rickshaw. Yet he continued his education alongside the work. "In the beginning, he thought he would have to leave his studies and drive a rickshaw," Archana says. "But gradually, he continued studying while working." He eventually completed his graduation. His routine revolved around driving the rickshaw while finding time to study. One day, he struck up a casual conversation with a fellow rickshaw puller who had noticed him studying diligently over the past few months. The man asked him, "Why don't you apply for a railway job?" Jagdish took the suggestion seriously. "He didn't know what to do next, but he applied for a railway job. He got the job and moved to Varanasi," Archana recalls. That one opportunity changed the family's circumstances. In Varanasi, he also found different ways to support the family while waiting for his career to settle. He painted boards and banners, made portraits and even wrote names and numbers on T-shirts. "He used to make portraits and earn some more income. That is how my father survived in the city," Archana says. Through Shiksha Saathi, Archana works to address learning gaps among children who attend school but often struggle to understand their lessons. But perhaps the biggest thing he brought back from that struggle was a belief that his children should have a different life. "My father did not want his children to grow up in the same circumstances he had," she says. A couple of months later, he brought his children to the city. They studied, built new lives for themselves, and for a while, it seemed the family had finally moved beyond those difficult years. When another challenge hit the family Archana was still young when her father passed away. His death left the family without the person who had worked so hard to give his children a more secure future. Her mother was supposed to take up his railway job, but she was not in a position to do so. With little support and no stable income, the family of five sisters and a brother found themselves facing financial difficulties once again. They continued living in the railway quarters, but meeting everyday expenses was becoming difficult. And with money running short, continuing their education — something their father had worked so hard to make possible — was now uncertain. The siblings had to find ways to support one another. It was during this difficult period that Archana's elder sister stepped in. "After a few months, my elder sister began earning and helped pay for groceries and tuition," she adds. "That gave us a means to continue studying and sometimes practising teaching along the way." For Archana, that support meant she could pursue her education despite the difficulties at home. She eventually went on to complete her graduation and post-graduation in Economics from Banaras Hindu University. Shiksha Saathi trains rural girls and women to become educators, creating opportunities for them to earn while supporting children in their communities. She had once hoped to become a professor, but without the right guidance and resources, that dream remained out of reach. Her own experiences had shown her how much education could change a family's circumstances, and how difficult it could be to pursue one's ambitions without the right support. Years later, she began noticing another problem , this time among children in her own extended family in rural Uttar Pradesh. They were attending school, but when Archana began asking them about their lessons, she found something troubling. 'Children struggled to recall their own lessons' Some of the children were already in Class 7, yet struggled to answer questions about what they had learnt in school. "That's when I realised that the quality of their education was not up to the mark," she says. As she looked more closely at the challenges children faced, she noticed another problem in the same villages. Girls in villages often had few opportunities to earn, even after studying. Coaching centres were limited, and travelling to cities was not an option for many families. "I realised that the girls were also struggling to find ways to earn because there was no tuition or coaching in the villages," Archana says. "So, we thought we should do something for them." In 2022, she started what was initially called Your Coaching. The organisation was formally registered as Shiksha Saathi in 2023. The idea was simple: if children could not travel to cities for better academic support, why not bring that support into their villages? 'Teachers, too, need training' Shiksha Saathi began offering affordable after-school coaching for children from Classes 1 to 12. The fees are kept low, starting at around Rs 100 for younger children and going up to Rs 1,100 for Class 12 students. Children who cannot afford the fees can still study with the others. But as the centres grew, Archana encountered another problem. By keeping coaching affordable and welcoming children who cannot pay, Shiksha Saathi aims to make academic support accessible to more rural families. A classroom could have a teacher and students, but that did not automatically mean good teaching was happening. At one centre, the team received a complaint about a teacher who was teaching English. When they tested him, they found that his own fundamentals were weak. For Archana, it was an important lesson. "We realised that simply teaching wasn't enough. We needed to train the teachers too," she says. That became the foundation of Shiksha Saathi's Educator Training Programme. Every six months, new batches of rural girls and women are trained to teach children according to their age and learning levels. More than 740 rural girls and women have now gone through the programme. The model began addressing two gaps at once: children received local academic support, while women got a chance to earn within their communities. For young women like Neetu, that opportunity also meant being able to continue their own education. 'I now pay for my own studies' At 19, Neetu became a teacher with Shiksha Saathi, a role she had never planned for. "I did it for myself and for the children in the village," she says. Coming from a Hindi-medium school, she was nervous at first. Shiksha Saathi provided classroom resources and six to seven months of training, gradually helping her gain confidence. Today, Neetu earns around Rs 6,000–7,000 a month, enough to pay for her own education and coaching. For Archana, every child who feels comfortable asking a question represents a chance to make learning more accessible. "I started paying for my own studies and coaching, so I no longer needed to take money from home," she says. For Neetu, the income means independence. She now hopes other girls can find the same confidence. "I want all girls to stand on their own feet and do something for themselves and help the younger children around them," she says. Her experience reflects why Archana wants more rural girls to become educators. "We give priority to girls because they should have the opportunity to learn, work and become financially independent," she says. And while women like Neetu are finding new opportunities through teaching, children in these centres are beginning to experience learning differently. From fearing Maths to enjoying it Among the children attending the centres is 10-year-old Riya, who has studied at Shiksha Saathi for three years. Maths, once her most difficult subject, is now her favourite. "When I used to study Maths before, I used to feel scared. Now, things have changed," she says. She credits her teachers, who take the time to explain concepts and let her ask about things she does not understand at school. Her parents, too, encourage her to keep studying. With support from her teachers at Shiksha Saathi, 10-year-old Riya has grown more confident in Maths, once her most difficult subject. And when asked what she wants to become, Riya has a clear answer: a teacher. For Archana, moments like these are why the work matters. She wants rural education to go beyond marks and school completion, helping children build the confidence to imagine possibilities beyond what they see around them. But making such opportunities available within villages also meant earning the trust of the communities themselves. 'The villagers support us now' In the beginning, getting communities to accept the centres was not always easy. People questioned girls travelling out, whether education was worth the cost, and whether women could work outside the home. But attitudes have slowly begun to change. In one village, that growing support came from a businessman living in Mumbai. After hearing about Shiksha Saathi's work, he offered his house as a space for children to attend classes and arranged water and other basic facilities for them. "The villagers support us a lot now," Archana says. "They tell us that their children are doing well." For Archana, such support matters because it shows that education is gradually becoming a community concern rather than an individual family's responsibility. Today, Shiksha Saathi has expanded across Bhadohi, Varanasi, Mirzapur, Prayagraj, Mau and Ghazipur. Giving more kids the chance to learn Shiksha Saathi now works across six districts, but Archana's vision goes beyond opening more coaching centres. Its youth competitions have reached over 9,000 children, while its 2025 initiative, Yuva Pratibha Parishad, encourages students to think about their ambitions, Plan A and Plan B, and how they want to contribute to society. "In villages, students have the talent, but they don't always have the opportunity," Archana says. "We want to give them the opportunities they are looking for." Community support has helped Shiksha Saathi expand its learning centres across six districts of Uttar Pradesh, bringing classes closer to children's homes. She hopes to reach more districts across Uttar Pradesh and make quality education affordable for families, a goal closely connected to her father's experience. Her father once pulled a rickshaw to support his family while continuing his studies. A stranger's advice eventually helped him secure a railway job, move to the city and give his children a different future. Archana hopes to help other children find opportunities that can shape their futures, just as education shaped her family's. And when children call out, "Archana ma'am!", she listens to their questions. For her, each question carries something her father worked hard to secure for his own children: the chance to learn. And she wants more children to have it. All images courtesy of Archana Jaisal

items.descriptionOriginal: You are driving home at night when a car approaches from the opposite direction. Its headlights are so bright that, for a few seconds, all you can see is a wall of white light. You cannot make out the divider, the edge of the road, or the cyclist who might be riding just ahead. You slow down, wait for the car to pass, and hope there is nothing in your path. Or perhaps you have been stuck in traffic when a vehicle suddenly appears behind you, flashing red and blue lights and honking as though everyone must move aside. If either of these situations sounds familiar, you know how frightening those few seconds can be. In August 2025, a Bengaluru commuter raised concerns on social media about an SUV fitted with flashing red and blue LED lights. The post caught the attention of the police. According to Bangalore Mirror, Jigani Police traced the vehicle and its occupant, removed the illegal lights and initiated legal action. The vehicle owner was also penalised. It was one example of a problem familiar to motorists across India. But what many drivers may not know is that there are already laws governing the lights vehicles can use. And in October 2025, the Supreme Court issued fresh directions to ensure those rules are taken seriously. The case behind that order began with a doctor's concern about the lives being lost on India's roads. Why a doctor took India's road safety problem to court Dr S. Rajaseekaran, an orthopaedic surgeon, had spent years seeing the consequences of road crashes. Injuries, lives lost, and families left dealing with the aftermath of accidents made him deeply concerned about road safety in India. In 2012, he approached the Supreme Court with a petition titled S. Rajaseekaran versus Union of India. His concern went far beyond headlights. He wanted the agencies responsible for safer roads, driver licensing, enforcement, emergency treatment and compensation to work together instead of functioning separately. For him, road accidents had become a national emergency that demanded coordinated action. The petition continued through years of hearings. Then, on 7 October 2025, a bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Viswanathan issued a series of directions addressing everyday dangers on Indian roads. These included unsafe pedestrian crossings, motorists riding without helmets, wrong-lane driving and dangerous overtaking. And among the problems the court addressed was something millions of drivers encounter after sunset: blinding headlights. Orthopaedic surgeon Dr S. Rajaseekaran approached the Supreme Court in 2012, seeking stronger coordination and accountability to make India's roads safer. Photograph: ( The Hindu ) What the Supreme Court said about blinding headlights Think about what happens when an unusually bright headlight shines directly into your eyes. Even if you are looking straight at the road, the glare can make it difficult to judge what is ahead. For a pedestrian, it may become harder to see an approaching vehicle or navigate the road safely. The Supreme Court recognised this danger. In its 7 October 2025 order , the court noted that high-intensity headlights, including those fitted on two-wheelers, can temporarily disorient oncoming drivers and pedestrians. It directed the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, state transport departments and traffic police to establish and enforce permissible limits for headlight brightness and beam angles. In simpler terms, authorities must ensure that headlights are bright enough to help drivers see the road, without directing excessive light into someone else's eyes. The court also called for these checks to be included in Pollution Under Control (PUC) testing and vehicle fitness certification, alongside targeted enforcement drives against non-compliant or modified headlights. But headlights were only part of the concern. The bench also directed strict enforcement of the ban on unauthorised red-blue flashing lights and illegal siren-like hooters. This includes action against vehicles using such equipment, as well as enforcement against its unauthorised sale. The court directed nationwide awareness campaigns so that motorists understand why these lights are dangerous. But why did the Supreme Court need to intervene when rules about vehicle lighting already existed? India already had headlight rules. So why is this still happening? The rules may sound complicated, but the idea behind them is fairly simple. Every vehicle needs lights that help its driver see clearly without putting other people in danger. Under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, Rule 105 deals with vehicle lamps, while Rule 106 requires headlight beams to meet prescribed safety standards. Section 52 of the Motor Vehicles Act also places restrictions on alterations that change a vehicle from the specifications approved by its manufacturer. Then there are the coloured lights that some vehicles use to demand attention on the road. Rule 108 restricts the use of multicoloured red, blue and white warning lights to vehicles specifically designated for emergency and disaster-management duties. Even authorised emergency vehicles cannot use their flashing lights and sirens whenever they wish. Under the Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017, these warning devices are meant to be used when responding to an emergency call or alarm. So a private vehicle cannot simply install flashing emergency-style lights and expect other drivers to clear the road. And a driver cannot assume that any brighter bulb will be suitable for their vehicle. To understand why, it helps to look at how headlights actually work. How replacing one bulb can make the road dangerous for someone else Imagine buying a powerful LED bulb to replace the original halogen bulb in your car. The idea seems reasonable. You want to see more clearly when driving at night. But headlights are designed to work as a complete system. The bulb, reflector or projector, and the angle at which the light falls are all important. A headlight housing designed for a particular halogen bulb may not direct light properly when a different type of LED or HID bulb is fitted inside it. Instead of concentrating light on the road, an unsuitable replacement can send some of it upwards, towards the eyes of approaching motorists. Even a properly designed headlight can cause glare if it is aimed incorrectly. Research by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) has found that effective headlights need to balance visibility for the driver with glare control for oncoming traffic. That is why brighter does not automatically mean safer. And it is also why the law does not treat every LED headlight as illegal. A factory-fitted LED system that complies with the applicable standards is permitted. An aftermarket replacement is not automatically an offence either, but it must meet the relevant safety requirements and vehicle alteration rules. The important question is whether the lighting system is compliant and safe for everyone sharing the road. In October 2025, the Supreme Court directed authorities to regulate headlight brightness and beam angles to reduce glare on Indian roads. Photograph: (AI-Generated collage) Can you be fined for bright headlights or flashing lights? For drivers, this is where the Supreme Court's directions become particularly relevant. Authorities have been asked to conduct targeted checks and take action against headlights that do not comply with the prescribed standards. But that does not mean every bright-looking headlight automatically attracts the same fine. Under Section 177 of the Motor Vehicles Act, when a violation has no separately prescribed penalty, the fine can extend to Rs 500 for a first offence and Rs 1,500 for a subsequent offence. Other violations may attract different penalties depending on the applicable legal provision. Unauthorised emergency-style flashing lights and illegal hooters can also invite enforcement action, including seizures and penalties. The court scheduled the case for a compliance review seven months after its October 2025 order. That was a date for reviewing progress, rather than a blanket seven-month deadline for states to introduce new headlight rules. Whether these directions make a difference on the road depends on how effectively authorities implement them. For vehicle owners, however, there is already a useful takeaway. Before changing your headlights, check that the replacement is compatible with your vehicle and meets the applicable standards. If the light seems unusually high or scattered, have its alignment checked. And if you encounter a private vehicle using unauthorised red-blue flashing lights or illegal hooters, the law provides grounds for enforcement action. Unauthorised red-blue flashing lights and siren-mimicking hooters are banned, with the court directing authorities to crack down on their use. Photograph: ( TNIE ) A few seconds of glare should never put someone's life at risk India recorded 1,72,890 road crash deaths in 2023, according to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. That included 35,221 pedestrians, people who were simply trying to walk or cross a road. There are many reasons why road accidents happen, and the available national data does not establish how many of these deaths were caused by headlight glare. But preventing unnecessary glare is one part of making roads safer. For the driver approaching an unfamiliar bend, the person cycling home after work, or the pedestrian trying to cross a poorly lit road, being able to see clearly matters. Thirteen years after Dr Rajaseekaran first approached the Supreme Court, there are now explicit judicial directions addressing dazzling headlights and unauthorised flashing lights. The next challenge is ensuring those directions are followed. Because when you are driving home at night, you should be able to trust that the headlights coming towards you will help another driver see the road, without taking away your ability to see it too.
